    Francophone Community Immigration Pilot

    Thank you for your interest in the Francophone Community Immigration Pilot (FCIP).

    Below is key information for employers in the Superior East region who wish to participate in the program.

    If you are an employer located in Superior East and would like to learn how to become a designated employer under the FCIP, please contact us using the form below.

    For all other inquiries, including general information about the FCIP, please visit the official IRCC website.

    Designated Employers

    • Magpie Relay Motel & Resort
    • A1 STOP INC - Esso
    • White River Bar and Grill
    • Select INN Motel
    • Superior Children's Centre
    • White River Motel

    Employer Requirements

    The process is straightforward, and we are here to help. Please fill out the form below.

    Next, take the required training. You must complete 2 free courses before you can apply for designation:

    1. onboarding training

    2. intercultural competency training

    You’ll get a certificate for completing these courses. Include them with your application to the community. Follow the link below:

    Take the required training

    Once you’re designated, you can offer jobs to eligible candidates.

    The Rural and Francophone Community Immigration Pilots don’t match candidates with jobs. You may find a candidate on your own, or a candidate may approach you.

    Hire a Candidate

    Once you’ve offered a job to a candidate, you need to complete a recommendation application and send it to the community.

    The recommendation application requires you to

    • show that you haven’t been able to fill the job with someone locally,
    • show that the job offer meets the pilot requirements
    • confirm that the candidate meets all of the requirements for the pilot
    • commit to connecting your candidate with immigrant settlement services in your community.

    You don’t need a labour market impact assessment.

    Click this link for further information:

    Submit a Recommendation for your Community

    Candidates who meet the requirements to apply for permanent residence may be eligible to apply for a temporary work permit.

    This work permit lets your candidate begin working while their permanent residence application is being processed.

    The work permit :

    • is only for these pilots
    • is valid for 2 years
    • is employer-specific, meaning the candidate can only work for you

    Click the following link for more details:

    Optional: Work Permit for Candidates
